dialogues.speaker: Yun Jin
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you. What brings you here today?

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: Oh, you! Who taught you to be so cheeky?

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: I'm not performing today, just dropping in to hear Mr. Liu Su tell a story — you know, to take my mind off things a bit.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: Our troupe will be rehearsing an old classic called "The Three Towers" in a few days' time.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: I'd like to adjust a few lines and the corresponding details in the performance, but I haven't really made up my mind about whether they should be changed or not.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: Would you mind hearing me out? If you have the time, of course.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: For example, there's a famous line that goes like this: "How gently do the clouds and flowers sway, as dancing winds meander through the vales. The half-moon is as a lovely face, and a glass raised to it moves the heart."

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: I'm not looking to change the first half, but the second, if sung as-is, feels like it is missing a little something.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: It would be great if I could add some actions that suit the scene — a raised bottle to indicate drinking, perhaps — and the set could be modified to match.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: There are quite a few more adjustments like that one, and though I would be personally more satisfied were we to change them, perhaps some older fans might prefer the way it was performed in the past.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: We don't have much time left to rehearse either, so there might be some issues with the timetable if we want to change the stage set and redo the stage movements.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: They are indeed. There are many outside factors to consider besides the script and performance themselves.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: Scriptwriting and performances are our greatest strengths at the Yun-Han Opera Troupe, and we love doing them, but beyond the stage... Well, that can get tricky.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: There are things we cannot control — whether the audiences will like our innovations, or if we can come to an amicable understanding with the organizers we're working with.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: But I see this as part of learning my role as Troupe Director — I'm already enjoying myself as a performer, and I'm sure these new challenges will present me with new kinds of delight as well.

choices.text: I'm sure you'll do just fine, Yun Jin.

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: Hehe. Thanks for your kind words. I'm more sure than ever that the road ahead will be a smooth one.

choices.text: I'll be cheering for you, Yun Jin!

response.speaker: Yun Jin
response.text: Well, then this is quite the coincidence. Would you like to have a seat?
